findings.title: A second account sees the previous traveler's private dashboard — account-independent query cache survives sign-out
findings.surface: Sign-out and sign-in; Inicio, Mi perfil, Mi Mundo and detail pages
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts that account B signing in in the same SPA within the cache retention period immediately receives A's cached private data while B's refetch runs. If that refetch fails, A's data remains available. This discloses travel history, profile and potentially gallery data on shared browsers, and contradicts the empty-new-account outcome; reload clears the in-memory cache but cannot undo disclosure.
findings.expected: R-001: "lands signed in on Inicio with their own empty profile"; request: "Cada usuario tendrá sus propios viajes, países, ciudades, fotografías, estadísticas y logros"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Sign-out clears the user's caches/client state".
reproduction_steps: Sign in as A and open Inicio and Mi perfil with saved private trips.
Use Mi cuenta to sign out without reloading the browser.
Register or sign in as B in the same tab and open Inicio/Mi perfil; inspect the cached data before refetch completion or when the refetch fails.
findings.evidence: App.js:24 creates one module-level QueryClient; :41 keeps its provider outside ClerkAuthProvider. lib/api.js:35 uses the supplied key without user identity. Home.jsx:13 uses ['home'], Profile.jsx:13-15 uses ['me'], ['stats'], ['trips']. AppShell.jsx:41,52 delegates sign-out to UserButton; no cache clearing occurs.

findings.title: Private travel photos remain accessible to signed-out link holders — file delivery has no privacy authorization
findings.surface: GET /api/files/{photo_id}; profile privacy switches
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: anyone who retains a photo URL from a previously public profile can continue fetching the original after the owner makes the profile private or hides photographs. The private-by-default owner's file also needs no authentication if its URL is forwarded. URLs are UUIDs, so enumeration is not established; disclosure to existing link holders and public caching are established by source, not runtime execution. Owners have no safe privacy revocation short of deleting the photo.
findings.expected: request: "Cada usuario podrá decidir qué información quiere compartir", "Perfil privado" and "Mostrar u ocultar fotografías"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Follow ... expired grants ... through every supported access path". Private media should be owner-authorized or covered by an explicit current share grant.
reproduction_steps: Publish a profile with a gallery photograph and retain the photograph's /api/files URL in another browser.
As owner, disable Mostrar fotografías and make the profile private.
As a signed-out visitor, open the retained file URL; the handler still returns the bytes.
findings.evidence: server.py:659 serve_file takes only photo_id, :660 looks up {'id': photo_id, 'is_deleted': False}, :663-665 returns bytes with 'Cache-Control': 'public, max-age=86400'. There is no viewer, owner, profile visibility or share grant check. file_url at :87-88 exposes this same stable URL everywhere.

findings.title: Public-profile visitors can retrieve hidden cities and photos — trip serialization leaks unrestricted share tokens
findings.surface: GET /api/public/users/{username}; /compartir/viaje/:token
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts that an owner who has shared a trip, exposes that trip on a public profile, and disables cities/photos still discloses city names in the public-profile response plus the bearer token that opens the full gallery. The visitor need not be an authorized recipient of the owner's separately generated share link. Turning the profile private does not revoke the leaked trip token. This leaks travel locations and private photographs; it is not merely a hidden UI section.
findings.expected: request: "Mostrar u ocultar ciudades", "Mostrar u ocultar fotografías" and "Compartir viajes individualmente"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Responses exclude secrets ... tokens and other users' data". A public listing must not distribute unrestricted share credentials or bypass visibility choices.
reproduction_steps: Create a trip with cities/photos, use Compartir once, and enable Compartir en mi perfil público.
Make the profile public but disable Mostrar ciudades and Mostrar fotografías.
Read its public profile response: trips still includes city names and the share token.
Open /compartir/viaje/<returned token> signed out; the city list and photographs are served.
findings.evidence: server.py:727-728 includes every public trip via enrich_trip(light=True), irrespective of show_cities/show_photos. enrich_trip :346 uses {**t}, preserving share_token, and :348 includes city names and ids. public_trip :761 checks only share_token, :765 enriches all cities, :769 returns gallery photos without consulting profile privacy. Public city records inside full trip enrichment also retain their share_token.

findings.title: Photo uploads cannot initialize with the supplied configuration — storage authentication is missing
findings.surface: Subir fotografías; Añadir ciudad/país with photos; profile avatar and trip cover
findings.observed: Third-party integrations: in the supplied configuration, unless deployment injects the absent storage credential at runtime, initialization sends a null authentication value and cannot obtain the required authenticated storage key. Every real photo/avatar/cover upload depends on that initialization; the UI reports failure and the required photo task cannot complete. This is a configuration-dependent source prediction, not an observed provider response. Supplying the runtime credential is the override that would change this conclusion.
findings.expected: request: "Las fotografías deben poder subirse y visualizarse" and "Almacenamiento de imágenes: almacenamiento externo preparado para producción"; checklist, Third-party integrations: "When every configuration source ... leaves a required provider value empty ... file the blocked feature".
reproduction_steps: Deploy using the repository's supplied backend configuration without injecting a storage credential.
Sign in and open a city.
Choose Subir fotografías and select a valid JPEG; initialization has no authentication value and the upload cannot complete.
findings.evidence: storage.py:15 posts initialization using only os.environ.get('EMERGENT_LLM_KEY'); :16 requires success and :17 requires storage_key. backend/.env configures database, Clerk and demo settings but has no storage authentication setting; no other app configuration supplies this value. server.py:580 calls storage.put_object for every upload, and :888-891 logs startup initialization errors without providing a fallback.

findings.title: Uploaded active SVG content can run on the application's backend origin — media validation trusts the supplied MIME type
findings.surface: POST /api/photos; GET /api/files/{photo_id}
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: an authenticated uploader can store a script-capable SVG labeled image/svg+xml and forward its file URL. When another traveler directly opens that URL as a document, the server serves active content on the API origin rather than a safe decoded image. This creates a stored-script execution path in the trusted application origin; access to credentials and user data depends on the browser's session state and same-origin deployment, but execution of attacker-supplied content in that origin follows from the response. No attack payload or runtime execution is asserted.
findings.expected: checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Trace upload ... validation on the server, type/size limits"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "untrusted HTML rendering". A photo uploader must not allow another user to execute untrusted active documents as trusted app-origin content.
reproduction_steps: As a signed-in user, upload a script-capable SVG as an image through the supported upload API.
Obtain its returned file URL.
Have another signed-in traveler open the file URL directly in the same-origin deployment; the response is an active SVG document, not sanitized or sandboxed media.
findings.evidence: server.py:571-574 accepts any declared image/* or video/*; :575 reads unvalidated bytes; :580 stores them unchanged. serve_file :664 serves original bytes with rec['content_type'], :665 supplies only a public cache header, with no attachment disposition, sandbox or content security policy.

findings.title: Moving a city leaves its photographs in the old trip's shared gallery — photo trip references are never reassigned
findings.surface: Editar ciudad → Viaje; trip gallery and shared trip gallery
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after moving a photographed city from trip A to trip B, B's count includes its photos but B's gallery omits them; A's gallery and existing shared trip link still return those photos even though A no longer contains the city. The owner can unintentionally leave photos publicly accessible on A after moving the city into a private B. This persistent cross-view/share mismatch follows from source; repair requires individually re-uploading/removing media rather than the offered move action.
findings.expected: request: "Quiero poder organizar el viaje por ciudades"; TripDetail.jsx:86 promises "Todas las fotos del viaje, incluidas las de sus ciudades"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Propagate ... changes to lists, detail pages, counts ... other views". Moving a city must consistently move its associated photo membership and sharing scope.
reproduction_steps: Create trips A and B, add a city and photographs under A, and share A.
Open the city → Editar → Viaje, select B and Guardar cambios.
Open B: its photo count includes the city but Galería del viaje does not.
Open A or its shared link: the moved city's photographs still appear.
findings.evidence: server.py:507-508 validates the new trip_id but :515 only updates the city document. Uploaded photos are denormalized with trip_id at :595-605; list_photos :624-625 filters by that stored trip_id alone, and public_trip :769 does the same. enrich_trip :338-341 instead counts photos using current city membership. CityEditDialog.jsx:19 permits changing or clearing trip_id.

findings.title: Documented null updates can disable an owner's dashboard and trips — nullable required values are persisted before unsafe reads
findings.surface: PUT /api/trips/{trip_id}; PUT /api/cities/{city_id}; Inicio/Mi perfil/Mis estadísticas
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: supported API clients sending country_codes:null receive a 500 after the trip has already been poisoned; subsequent trip/list and applicable home reads fail on the same stored value. Sending name:null for a city persists successfully but breaks /stats and /home for that user. The normal UI cannot open the broken data to repair it in some of these paths, so core dashboard/history access requires a corrective API call or developer help. This is a complete source trace, not an executed request.
findings.expected: checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Compare request/response contracts ... omitted/empty/null values" and "partial updates preserve omitted fields"; checklist, code-quality: runtime paths avoid unhandled 5xx. Explicitly accepted null updates must either have safe clearing semantics or be rejected before persistence.
reproduction_steps: Using the documented API as an authenticated owner, update an existing trip with country_codes set to null.
Open that trip and Mi perfil; enrichment now iterates null and fails.
Alternatively update a city's name to null, which the documented schema allows, then open Inicio or Mis estadísticas.
findings.evidence: server.py:329 permits country_codes=None in TripUpdate; clean_trip :362 skips normalization for None; update_trip :392-395 persists it before enrich_trip :347 iterates t.get('country_codes', []). That iteration fails for stored null. CityUpdate :433 permits name=None; :506-515 persists it; stats.py:60 then calls c['name'].strip(). The supplied OpenAPI explicitly advertises these null values.

findings.title: Travelers cannot save offered territory cities — geocoder territory codes are incompatible with the 195-country validator
findings.surface: Añadir ciudad → worldwide CitySearch; POST /api/cities
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: when the world geocoder returns San Juan with PR (or other territory-specific ISO codes outside the reference list), the UI offers and selects it but saving always fails 'País no válido'. The selected result offers no country correction. Territory-city travelers cannot complete the promised worldwide-search registration through the normal flow; no provider response was executed, so the trigger is explicitly the geocoder returning its territory code.
findings.expected: request: "Buscador mundial de ciudades", "Las ciudades estarán vinculadas a su país correspondiente" and "193 miembros de Naciones Unidas y los dos Estados observadores". Inferred consistent contract: a valid territory city must map to its sovereign reference country without increasing the 195-country denominator; it must not be offered as a selectable but unsavable city.
reproduction_steps: Search worldwide for San Juan and choose the Puerto Rico result whose country_code is PR.
Fill visit dates and choose Guardar ciudad.
Whether marking the country too or saving only the city, backend validation rejects PR; the selected country's field is not editable.
findings.evidence: search_cities :226-228 forwards all geocoder country_code values without mapping/filtering. create_city :475 calls check_country, whose :91-94 rejects codes absent from COUNTRY_BY_CODE. The reference list includes US (countries_data.py:181) but not PR; likewise FR exists but GP/MQ do not. CitySearch.jsx:38 selects those results unchanged and AddCityDialog.jsx:34 sends their code unchanged; non-manual selected countries cannot be changed (:77-81).

findings.title: Deleting a trip makes its direct photographs inaccessible despite a preservation promise — detached media has no gallery or reassignment flow
findings.surface: Eliminar viaje; Inicio recent photographs; absent unassigned photo library
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: deleting a trip with direct gallery uploads preserves records but removes their only navigable gallery. Unlinked photographs cannot be opened full-screen, edited, reassigned or deleted through the UI; only up to 12 recent thumbnails may appear on Inicio, pointing nowhere. Owners lose practical access to their photo history despite the explicit assurance; records can be recovered only through direct API/developer work or pre-retained file links, not the normal interface.
findings.expected: The app's deletion confirmation: "Las ciudades y fotos se conservarán sin viaje asignado"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Handle children on parent deletion by cascade, refusal or reassignment" and checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: preserved work remains accessible. Keeping bytes but orphaning them from every usable gallery does not preserve their use for the owner.
reproduction_steps: Create a trip with no cities and upload 20 photographs directly to Galería del viaje.
Choose Eliminar and accept the message promising photos will be preserved.
Return to Inicio/Mi perfil: the trip gallery is gone, there is no unassigned-photo library, and recent orphan thumbnails link to #.
Try to open or organize the preserved older photos through the UI; no destination exists.
findings.evidence: TripDetail.jsx:25 promises 'Las ciudades y fotos se conservarán sin viaje asignado.' server.py:401 deletes the trip and :403 sets its photos' trip_id=None. Photos uploaded directly to a trip have city_id=None (:589-605). PhotoGallery.jsx:35-39 can only request a city or trip gallery; App.js:33-36 has no standalone photo-library route. Home.jsx:88 routes an unlinked photo to '#', and server.py:701 caps recent images at 12.

findings.title: Clicking Rome opens Vaticano instead of Italy — tiny-country fallback captures a 0.35-degree radius
findings.surface: Mi Mundo globe country click
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a click in central Rome (41.90,12.50), inside the supplied Italy polygon, returns VA because its coordinate distance from the VA reference is 0.05 < 0.35. Travellers selecting Italy around Rome receive Vaticano's name, status and registration action instead. The same overbroad hit area affects other microstates; selecting Italy elsewhere or using the picker is a safe recovery.
findings.expected: R-025 (derived): clicking a tiny country opens 'that country's own information panel'; request: 'Al pulsar sobre un país se abrirá una ventana con su información'. Country identity must follow the clicked boundary, not merely proximity to another country.
reproduction_steps: Open Mi Mundo and zoom into Rome.
Click central Rome east of Vaticano, around 41.90,12.50.
The click handler chooses VA and opens Ciudad del Vaticano, not Italia.
findings.evidence: WorldGlobe.jsx:94 selects any missing-feature place with Math.hypot(p.lat - at.lat, p.lng - at.lng) < 0.35 instead of testing its boundary. countries_data.py:47 places VA at 41.9,12.45. frontend/public/countries.geojson includes Italy but no VA feature. MiMundo.jsx:57-59 renders the panel for the returned code.

findings.title: Public share responses disclose city sharing credentials — public serializers return stored share_token fields
findings.surface: GET /api/public/cities/{token}; GET /api/public/trips/{token}
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts signed-out share recipients receive stored sharing credentials, including independent city links inside a shared trip. A recipient can retain a separately shared city's token even when only given a trip link, then continue opening that city after the owner moves it out of the trip. Email and personal comments are excluded, but the public projection is not the promised allowed-field boundary. Scope is share-link recipients, not arbitrary account access; no runtime request was made.
findings.expected: R-031 (derived): the public response 'carries no owner share token, email or unshared photo'. Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: responses exclude tokens and keep delegated access scoped to the intended resource. Explicitly project public fields for both the city and nested city records.
reproduction_steps: Create a city, use Compartir galería, and attach it to a trip.
Share the trip and open its link signed out.
Inspect the public trip response: its nested city contains the independent city share_token.
Move the city to another trip; the recipient still has a standalone link to it. The direct public city response also echoes its own token.
findings.evidence: server.py:814 excludes only _id, user_id and comments from the shared city; :816 passes it to enrich_city, which spreads **c at :470, retaining share_token. :825 enriches a shared trip, and :826-828 strip only user_id/comments from its nested cities, retaining each city's share_token. By contrast :784 explicitly strips the token in public_view.

findings.title: City edits accept a cover from another gallery or a deleted file — validation checks ownership only
findings.surface: PUT /api/cities/{city_id}, cover_photo_id and trip_id update
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts an owner's update assigning city A a deleted photo id or a photo belonging to city B succeeds, and an accompanying trip reassignment moves A's photos. A deleted photo then renders a missing cover; another gallery's photo misrepresents A. This violates the promised whole rejection of an invalid cover and requires a corrective edit; owner isolation itself is enforced.
findings.expected: R-032 (derived): validate 'the proposed cover photo against the stored gallery before moving any photo', and an invalid update leaves city, gallery and cover unchanged. A cover must be a live image in that city's gallery, not simply any file the caller owns.
reproduction_steps: Create two cities A and B and upload an image to B.
As the owner, submit PUT /api/cities/<A> with B's photo id as cover_photo_id and a different owned trip_id.
The handler accepts the foreign-gallery cover and moves A's photos rather than refusing the update.
Repeat with the id of a deleted owned photo: the accepted cover URL cannot be served.
findings.evidence: server.py:531 tests only {'id': data['cover_photo_id'], 'user_id': profile['user_id']}; :539-541 repeat that same check. Neither requires city_id, is_deleted=False, kind=gallery or media_type=image. :538 moves gallery trip associations before :545 stores the accepted cover. enrich_city at :468 uses that id directly, while serve_file at :712 excludes deleted files.

findings.title: A temporary flag outage leaves the globe's blue fallback cached for a week — incomplete tiles receive long-lived success headers
findings.surface: Mi Mundo globe; GET /api/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg?v=...
findings.observed: Third-party integrations: if a flag download fails during render, the backend avoids its internal tile cache, but the browser/proxy is explicitly allowed to reuse the fallback JPEG for 604800 seconds (7 days). Returning to the same zoom after the provider recovers therefore need not issue another request or retry the flag. Travellers keep seeing a flat cyan visited country instead of its flag; clearing caches is not an ordinary in-app recovery. This is a source prediction, not a measured outage.
findings.expected: R-029 (derived): a failed flag download must not become a permanent failure and repeating the tile must try the flag again. Request: 'Que conforme voy ampliando el mundo se vean los colores en 4k'. Incomplete fallback responses must remain retryable throughout the HTTP cache path.
reproduction_steps: Open a visited country's globe tile while its flag provider fails.
Let the endpoint return its fallback JPEG with the current cache header.
After the provider recovers, revisit the same tile/zoom with normal browser caching.
The cached fallback can be reused for seven days without reaching the server retry logic.
findings.evidence: tiles.py:111-114 marks a missing flag incomplete and paints a cyan fallback; :76-78 returns only its bytes without caching them in _tiles. server.py:224-228 cannot distinguish that incomplete result and always sends 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800'. WorldGlobe.jsx:29 uses the same URL for the same tile and visited set.

findings.title: Flag-provider failures still serialize long retries within each tile — failed parallel prefetches are fetched again in the polygon loop
findings.surface: GET /api/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg with multiple visited countries
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: when several relevant flag requests time out, prefetch is parallel but rendering then retries those same failed requests one polygon at a time. For three intersecting countries with one polygon each and 20-second timeouts, the flag path is approximately 20 + 3×20 = 80 seconds, excluding imagery; multipart countries can add more retries. Users zooming during a flag outage wait for tiles, and requests occupy synchronous worker threads far beyond the promised parallel first render. No latency was measured.
findings.expected: R-029 (derived): flags for visited countries on a tile are fetched in parallel so response time is not the sum of flag fetches. Checklist, Third-party integrations: delayed/unavailable dependencies need bounded, usable failure handling. Reuse the current render's prefetch results, retrying failures on a later request rather than serially during the same render.
reproduction_steps: Mark several countries in one low-zoom tile visited.
Request that tile while their flag downloads time out.
Trace the parallel prefetch completion followed by the per-polygon _flag calls.
Each failed flag is downloaded again sequentially before the fallback JPEG is returned.
findings.evidence: tiles.py:89 finishes _pool.map(_flag, needed); failed _flag calls return None without recording an attempt at :61-62. The subsequent loop over each polygon at :98-111 calls _flag(code) again. Each failing call has timeout=20 at :58, including repeated polygons for the same country.

findings.title: Backend starts without required uniqueness after an index error — startup logs and suppresses index-creation failures
findings.surface: Backend startup; POST /api/visited
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if the unique index cannot be created (for example a store containing historical duplicate visits), awaiting ensure_indexes still reports successful startup. Two new simultaneous submissions for the same user and country can both pass the precheck and persist duplicate records. Lists and passports then show duplicates; a delete removes only one record. This is conditional on an index-creation error, not a claim that the deployed database currently has one.
findings.expected: R-033 (derived): startup 'ensures the unique indexes it relies on' and simultaneous identical visits leave one stored record. Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: uniqueness must be store-enforced, not only checked before insertion. Do not serve writes while that guarantee is unavailable.
reproduction_steps: Start with a database where the required user_country unique index fails to build, such as a migrated collection containing duplicates.
Start the backend: the exception is logged but startup completes.
Send two simultaneous visits for a different, previously unvisited country under one account.
Both prechecks can see no record and both inserts succeed without the required index.
findings.evidence: server.py:52 declares the unique (user_id,country_code) index. ensure_indexes at :71-74 catches every creation exception and only logs it; startup at :946 awaits this fail-open helper. create_visited at :293-295 uses a non-atomic precheck followed by insert_one at :280.

findings.title: City lookup keeps selectable results for the previous query after a failure — new searches never clear the result state
findings.surface: Añadir ciudad / shared CitySearch component
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: after a successful Paris lookup, changing the query to Roma retains Paris buttons during the next lookup and indefinitely if it fails. The error says the service is unavailable but the results below still look selectable for Roma. Travellers can register the wrong city's name and coordinates, or must inspect and redo the selection. A new successful lookup or clearing the box is a safe recovery; stale network completions themselves are correctly guarded.
findings.expected: Checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: pending/failure states and available controls must reflect the actual operation. R-027's failure/clearing outcome supports a usable city-search recovery. Results must correspond to the displayed query, not a previous successful query.
reproduction_steps: Open Añadir ciudad and search Paris; wait for results.
Replace the query with Roma without clearing it to fewer than two characters.
During the debounce/request, or if the Roma request fails, observe that the Paris result buttons remain.
Selecting a retained button submits the earlier Paris city, not a Roma result.
findings.evidence: CitySearch.jsx:14 clears res only for queries shorter than two characters; :17-18 begins a lookup without clearing res. :21 replaces res only on success, whereas :22 only sets error on failure. :38-43 continues to render the retained results and lets onSelect use them.

findings.title: Concurrent city-and-country saves report failure after saving the city — country uniqueness errors occur after an irreversible city insert
findings.surface: POST /api/cities with mark_country_visited=true; Añadir ciudad
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: with the unique index working, two tabs saving different cities in the same not-yet-visited country can each insert their city and then both see no country visit. One add_visited fails on the unique key after its city is committed, producing an unhandled 500. That tab never receives the city id, never uploads its selected photos, and retry creates another city record. The loss is misleading save failure, missing attachments and duplicate travel records, recoverable through manual cleanup.
findings.expected: R-033 (derived): concurrent identical country visits must be refused without duplicates. Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: multi-document operations must not leave unexplained half-written state, and retries preserve operation identity. A city-plus-country save should return the saved city or fail without leaving an unacknowledged city behind.
reproduction_steps: In two tabs for one account, open Añadir ciudad for two cities in an unvisited country.
In both, choose Sí, marcar país y guardar at nearly the same time.
Interleave the requests so both cities insert and both country-existence checks run before either country insert.
One country insert loses the unique-index race after its city was saved; retry the apparent failed save and see the second city record created.
findings.evidence: create_city inserts the city at server.py:505 before :507 checks whether to mark the country visited and :508 calls add_visited. The required unique index is at :52; add_visited's insert at :280 has no DuplicateKeyError handling. AddCityDialog.jsx:41-47 treats any failed response as failure and keeps the form for retry, without the committed city id.

findings.title: Owners cannot withdraw a shared gallery or trip link without deleting their records — no token revocation operation exists
findings.surface: City/trip sharing controls; public share routes
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: once an owner presses Compartir, the city/gallery link remains valid permanently until the city itself is deleted; making the profile private, turning off public-trip visibility, or pressing Compartir again cannot invalidate it. Travellers who accidentally share private memories or later withdraw permission cannot safely revoke access while keeping their work. This is a missing recovery capability rather than a claim that deliberately shared links should obey profile visibility.
findings.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: delegated/shared access must respect revocation; request: 'Cada usuario podrá decidir qué información quiere compartir' and private by default. R-031 refers to an unknown or revoked token returning none of the record. Owners need a way to invalidate a previously issued link without destroying their travel history.
reproduction_steps: Create a city/gallery and use Compartir galería to issue its link.
Decide to stop sharing while retaining the city and photos.
Look for a revoke/unshare action or API operation: none exists; sharing again returns the same token.
Open the original link signed out after setting the profile private: the city still loads.
findings.evidence: server.py:578-579 always reuses or creates a city token and stores it; :811 authorizes a public read solely by that token. CityUpdate (:451-459) has no share/revoke field and there is no DELETE share handler in the route inventory. Trip sharing similarly stores a token at :429-430; switching is_public off in update_trip does not clear it. CityDetail.jsx:56-59 and TripDetail.jsx:54-58 expose sharing and deletion but no stop-sharing action.

findings.title: Large galleries silently lose their tail from owner and shared views — fixed 200/500-item caps have no pagination
findings.surface: Private city/trip galleries; signed-out shared city/trip gallery
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a city with 201 uploaded photos reports photo_count=201 but its owner gallery can open/edit only the first 200. At 501 photos the public gallery permanently omits the last photo and claims there are 500 files, with no next page or show-all action. Uploads can accumulate past these caps in ordinary batches, so stored and shared travel content becomes inaccessible through the supported galleries. Originals remain stored, but users cannot browse or manage the hidden tail normally.
findings.expected: Request: 'Quiero poder subir tantas fotografías como quiera' and 'Compartir la ciudad o galería mediante un enlace'. R-030: the share view shows the shared city's photos. Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: pagination reaches the last record and exposes truncation; counts match the represented rows.
reproduction_steps: Upload 201 valid photos to one city in several batches.
Open its detail page: the total includes 201, but only 200 gallery items are fetched and no next page exists.
Accumulate 501 photos, issue Compartir galería, and open the link signed out.
Only 500 photos and a 500-file label are returned/displayed; there is no way to load the remainder.
findings.evidence: server.py:652 defaults private photo retrieval to 200 and :660 returns only that many without offset/cursor. PhotoGallery.jsx:38-39 never supplies a limit or requests a later page. Public city/trip queries at server.py:815 and :829 cap at 500 and return no continuation; Shared.jsx:54 renders only d.photos and its truncated length. enrich_city at server.py:470 counts the entire gallery.

findings.title: Saving a city silently drops photos after the first 50 selected — the upload loop slices the batch and returns success
findings.surface: POST /api/photos; Añadir ciudad multi-photo upload
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: selecting 51 otherwise valid images in Añadir ciudad saves the city and first 50 images, silently ignores image 51, and closes the dialog with a success toast. That traveller reasonably believes the selected memories were all stored. The omitted original can be reuploaded if the user notices, so this is recoverable content loss rather than destruction of originals.

findings.title: Experienced travellers wait tens of seconds for cold globe tiles — each intersecting country's flag is downloaded serially before a tile can respond

A read-only bbox calculation against countries50.geojson:1 finds 102 catalogue sovereign codes intersecting z=2,x=2,y=1 (longitude 0..90, latitude 0..66.51), so a traveller with 20 of those visited causes 20 cold flag fetches in one tile.

findings.title: The most-visited-country tile rewards cities and planned trips rather than actual visits — unrelated record types are summed
findings.surface: Mis estadísticas → País más visitado
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: one completed Italy trip with four cities contributes five Italy occurrences; two completed Germany trips with one city each contribute four Germany occurrences. This materially misstates a requested personal metric but does not destroy the history; source prediction, not measured behavior.
findings.expected: request: "País más visitado"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Establish ... eligible records". Inferred meaning: adding cities inside one visit does not create additional visits to that country, and an unvisited pending trip is not a completed visit. Thus one Italy trip covering four cities is one country visit, while two distinct Germany trips are two visits.
reproduction_steps: Record one completed Italy trip with four city records.
Record two completed Germany trips, each with one city.
Open Mis estadísticas → País más visitado: Italy wins the implemented counter despite fewer actual country visits.

findings.title: Planned future trips count as time already spent traveling — days statistic sums every full trip interval
findings.surface: Mis estadísticas → días viajando
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: a user who has never traveled but creates a future pending 10-day trip is immediately credited with 10 días viajando. The tile overstates completed travel rather than distinguishing planned days, misleading the user's requested history statistics; this is recoverable by deleting the plan, which is not a correct way to maintain a travel organizer.
findings.expected: request: "Días viajando" shown automatically in "Mis estadísticas"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Establish ... eligible records ... overlapping/excluded groups". Open Mis estadísticas without changing status or traveling.
The days tile is 10 rather than zero.

Open an existing photographed city while only /photos fails: the gallery says Aún no hay fotografías.

findings.title: City search shows results for an older query after users change it — in-flight requests have no cancellation or freshness guard

findings.title: Popular cities are omitted in favor of less-visited ones — aggregation limits by user-id array ordering before counting travelers
findings.surface: GET /api/explore → top_cities; Explorar city popularity list
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: when more than 24 distinct cities exist, the database selects cities by lexicographic user-id values rather than traveler count. A two-traveler city can be discarded in favor of 24 single-traveler cities whose ids sort later; Python's later count-sort cannot restore the discarded popular city. The community is shown materially wrong recommendations for the stated popularity criterion. Source-predicted data ordering, not executed aggregation.

Have travelers with higher-sorting ids record 24 different cities, one eligible traveler each.
Open Explorar → Ciudades → Más visitadas por la comunidad.
City A can be missing because the limit was applied to user-id ordering before popularity sorting.

findings.title: Quick photo moves revert after reload — overlapping reorder saves can overwrite the user's latest order

Let the request for the first order [B,A,C] complete after the second [B,C,A].
Reload the city gallery: the stored order can revert to the earlier intent rather than keeping [B,C,A].

findings.title: Owners cannot stop sharing a city or trip without deleting it — permanent share tokens have no revoke or rotation path
findings.surface: Compartir viaje / Compartir galería; shared links and privacy controls
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: after sharing a city or trip, the owner cannot withdraw access from old recipients or a forwarded link. Making the profile private, hiding photos, or disabling the trip's public-profile switch does not stop that token. Pressing Compartir again redistributes the same grant. The only available revocation is deleting the entire city/trip, which destroys the record/gallery access and is not a safe privacy control. This is a missing revocation capability proven by the complete route/control inventory, not a claim that any specific recipient accessed the link.

Inferred privacy table stake: an owner can stop a previously authorized share without destroying their own travel record and gallery.

Attempt to stop sharing while retaining the travel record: inspect Editar, profile privacy and Compartir.
Make the profile private and disable public-trip visibility, then reopen the old share URL.
It continues to return the shared content; no revoke or new-link action is available.

TripUpdate/CityUpdate schemas have no revocation setting and there is no revoke/rotate share route. The corresponding UI exposes only Compartir/Compartir galería, editing and whole-record deletion; profile privacy is not consulted by these shared handlers.

findings.title: Keyboard users tab through hidden background controls instead of the photo editor — fullscreen overlay never takes or traps focus
findings.surface: Fullscreen gallery lightbox/photo editor

Opening a fullscreen photo editor must move keyboard focus into that editor and keep Tab navigation within its visible controls until closing.

Press Tab to reach the fullscreen photo-editor controls.
Focus remains in the background gallery rather than entering/staying within the overlay; hidden controls can be activated.

findings.title: One newly registered traveler can receive duplicate profiles during startup — unique-index creation runs after writes become available
findings.surface: Fresh deployment startup; lazy profile creation on first authenticated requests
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: on a fresh database when index building is slower than startup's storage initialization, two first requests for the same authenticated user can both see no profile and insert separate profiles before the unique user_id index exists. Subsequent index creation then fails on those duplicates and is only logged, leaving both profiles and no constraint. Different stable profile ids can be returned for the same traveler and social references can attach to whichever record a read selects. Scope is first-start/index-failure timing; no claim is made that existing correctly indexed databases reproduce it.
findings.expected: R-002: "creates a user with a stable unique id and one profile owned by that id" and "duplicate registration must be refused by the store, not only by the form"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "A check before insert alone races". Before provisioning is available, profile uniqueness must already be enforced and failed constraint initialization must not leave the app serving unconstrained writes.
reproduction_steps: Start the supplied app against a fresh database under conditions where creating indexes is still pending when startup returns.
Register a user and issue concurrent first /api/me and /api/home requests for that same authenticated identity.
Both profile lookups can precede either insertion while the unique user_id constraint is absent.
Observe from the source sequence that two random profile records can commit and the later unique-index failure is logged instead of blocking service.
findings.evidence: startup :886 launches ensure_indexes as a background task and never awaits it before accepting traffic. ensure_indexes :70 builds unique indexes and :71-72 merely logs failures. get_profile :116 checks then :132 inserts a new random profile; no atomic upsert is used. findings_minor.title: Keyboard users cannot activate globe city labels or flag pins — clickable divs have no focus or keyboard behavior
findings_minor.surface: WorldGlobe city labels and country flag pins
findings_minor.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: keyboard-only travellers cannot focus or activate the city-label or tiny-country flag-pin shortcuts shown on the globe. The onclick handlers work only through pointer activation, with no focusable semantic control. The same records remain reachable from Mis ciudades/Mis países, so this is a minor shortcut-accessibility failure rather than total loss of the core logging task.
findings_minor.expected: Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: shared interaction must work for keyboard and assistive use; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: a navigation reference must reach its intended destination. Use keyboard-operable links/buttons or equivalent focus and activation behavior for globe labels.
reproduction_steps: Open Mi Mundo and zoom in so saved city labels appear.
Use Tab to try to focus a city label, then Enter to open its city.
The div is absent from keyboard navigation and has no keyboard activation handler.
Use Mis ciudades instead to reach the record through the alternative supported route.
findings_minor.evidence: WorldGlobe.jsx:101 creates a div; :104 and :107 assign only onclick for city labels and country pins. :109 sets pointer-events and cursor, but no tabIndex, role or keyboard handler is set; the descendants are spans/images rather than buttons or links. MiMundo.jsx:72 wires these pointer-only city labels to /ciudades/:id navigation.

findings_minor.title: Clearing an in-flight city search leaves a permanent spinner — stale-response cleanup never resets the empty-query loading state
findings_minor.surface: CitySearch input in Añadir ciudad, Editar perfil and Explorar
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source prediction. Type a query, wait for its request to start, and erase it before the reply. Cleanup invalidates the reply, while the empty-query branch leaves loading true forever. The empty input continues showing the spinner even after the old request completes. The user can still start a new search to recover, so this is minor misleading feedback rather than blocked saving.
findings_minor.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve initial, empty, pending, success, failure ... states against the actual operation state" and "failure ending loading." Clearing a city query should clear its loading/error indicators too.
reproduction_steps: In Añadir ciudad, type Roma and wait at least 350 ms for the request to begin.
Before its response arrives, erase the entire query.
Wait for the old request to finish: the spinner is not cleared until another sufficiently long query completes.
findings_minor.evidence: CitySearch.jsx:17 sets loading true when a request starts; :25 marks it stale on input change; :23 then suppresses loading=false for that stale request. The new effect's q.trim().length<2 branch at :14 only clears results and never resets loading or error.

findings_withdrawn.title: Public profiles reveal hidden country information — privacy gates are not applied to public trips or achievement payloads
findings_withdrawn.reason: The request independently permits sharing individual trips, and the UI describes the country/city privacy switches as controlling the profile's globe, country list and visited-city section. Public-trip country fields and visible achievements are not sufficient to prove that this intentionally separate publication violates the promised privacy policy. Removing this finding rather than assuming global suppression overrides individually published content.
